request: 가능한 베스트버젼의 reels (너가 가장 자신있게 만드는) 를 보여줘 · Style: swiss-signal · Register: rich
pathReason: The film shows a 3D Earth, the Moon and the ocean moving, which needs drawn objects rather than type alone; a vertical reel always takes the stage path.
idea: A turning Earth shows why the ocean bulges on the side away from the Moon as well as under it, which is why most coasts see two high tides a day.
audience: Curious people scrolling short videos who have never been told why there are two tides
channel: Instagram Reels, watched vertically with sound
formatReason: Reels play full screen in portrait.

beats.onScreen: A large Earth rises from the bottom of the frame against a star field, its ocean catching a key light, the question above it
beats.motion: Slow push-in as the Earth rises and turns
beats.sound: The intro starts; a soft hit on the first cut

beats.purpose: Step one: the Moon pulls the near water
beats.onScreen: The Moon slides in at the top, pull arrows run from it to the Earth, and the ocean shell swells toward it into a near bulge, with a distance readout
beats.motion: Camera trucks up to put Moon and Earth in one frame; the ocean shell swells toward the Moon
beats.sound: Hats come in; a rise into the turn
beats.hero: The ocean swells toward the Moon

beats.purpose: Step two, the turn: a second bulge on the far side
beats.onScreen: The camera orbits round the Earth and the far side of the ocean swells out as well, until the shell is a stretched egg with one bulge toward the Moon and one away from it
beats.motion: Orbit a quarter turn around the Earth while the far bulge grows; the largest change of the film
beats.sound: The drop lands with a hit on the cut
beats.hero: The far side of the ocean swells out

beats.purpose: Result: a coast spins through both bulges
beats.onScreen: The Earth spins under the two bulges; a bright marker on a coast passes high, low, high, low, while a tide-height curve draws itself beside it
beats.motion: Camera cranes down to look along the equator as the Earth turns; the curve draws in step
beats.sound: The groove continues; taps as the marker hits each high tide
beats.hero: The coast marker rides through both bulges

beats.purpose: Recap: two crests a lunar day
beats.onScreen: Earth and Moon small in the frame with the stretched ocean between them, the orbit drawn as a ring, the final line in the caption band
beats.motion: Camera pulls back to the whole system
beats.hero: The camera pulls back to the whole Earth and Moon system

story.expect: The Moon pulls the sea toward it, so there should be one high tide, on the side facing the Moon.
story.turn: The ocean also swells out on the side facing away from the Moon, so there are two bulges.
story.payoff: Every coast turns through both bulges each lunar day, which is why the tide comes in twice.

protagonist.name: Earth's ocean
protagonist.look: A deep teal water shell around a dark rocky Earth, filling most of the frame, glinting in a single key light

acts.action: Rises into frame, calm and round
Swells toward the Moon into one bulge
Swells out on the far side too, into a stretched egg
Holds its two bulges while the Earth spins under it
Sits stretched between Earth and Moon as the camera pulls away

subject.name: Two tides a day
specifics: The Moon's pull is stronger on the near ocean than on the Earth's centre, and weaker on the far ocean, so the water stretches both ways
A coast turns through both bulges in one lunar day of about 24 h 50 min
So high tides come about 12 h 25 min apart

typePlan.hierarchy: Archivo display for the question, Archivo headline for each step, MesloLGS NF labels on the bodies and readouts

palette.role: the pull arrows and the coast marker
state in progress: the tide curve

layers: The Earth, its ocean shell and the Moon
Readout panels and labels pinned to the bodies

sound.plan: A house groove that builds under the question and the Moon's pull, drops on the turn as the far bulge appears, and settles into an outro with a cadence on the recap.

events.on: the far bulge reaches full size
the coast marker reaches the first high tide
the coast marker reaches the second high tide

lines: Why does the sea rise twice a day?
The far side swells as well.

inventions: Two tides a day: the choice of subject and all five copy lines
The labels and readouts on screen, written from the real figures: 384,400 km to the Moon, a lunar day of about 24 h 50 min
ambition: Make the far bulge a genuine surprise: the camera orbits as it grows so the viewer sees the water stretch away from the Moon in 3D, lit like a real planet, with every label pinned to the body it names.
